title: Infuriating Google commercial imagines the founding fathers embracing AI
slides: That Google ad with the founding fathers—why does it infuriate so many?
It shows Washington and Jefferson using AI to draft the Constitution.
Historians actually say the founders feared centralized power, not embraced it.
Your own historical arguments now risk being dismissed as outdated.
Check the ad's source material before citing AI in your next debate.
thread_text:
1. Why the ad infuriates

Historians say the founders actually feared centralized power, not embraced it.

2. Google’s historical rewrite

The ad shows Washington and Jefferson using AI to draft the Constitution — a myth.

3. Your arguments at risk

If you cite that ad, your historical claims get dismissed as outdated.

4. The real cost of shortcuts

Using AI without checking sources can destroy your credibility instantly.

5. Check before you cite

Open the ad’s source material and compare it to the founding documents. Have you?

instagram.caption:
A founding father who handed Washington a quill might be rolling in his grave — because Google’s ad shows them drafting the U.S. Constitution with AI. Historians actually say the founders feared centralized power, not enthusiastically outsourced the country’s founding to it 📜

The ad rewrites a core historical truth to sell a product. If you cite that commercial as a shortcut, your own claims get dismissed as outdated or fabricated.

Your reputation depends on source-checking, not vibes. Have you opened the ad’s citations and compared them to federalist papers — or just hit ‘post’? 🔍
